lines.text: Blood enters the glomerulus through the afferent arteriole and leaves through the efferent arteriole.
Net filtration pressure = glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure (~55 mmHg) − Bowman's capsule pressure (~15 mmHg) − plasma oncotic pressure (~30 mmHg) ≈ 10 mmHg.
GFR ≈ 125 mL/min (≈180 L/day). Renal plasma flow ≈ 650 mL/min, so filtration fraction ≈ 20%.
Constricting the efferent arteriole raises glomerular pressure and GFR; constricting the afferent arteriole lowers both.
Reabsorbs ~65% of filtered Na+ and water, all filtered glucose and amino acids, ~80% of bicarbonate.
Reabsorption is iso-osmotic: tubular fluid stays ~300 mOsm/kg.
3. Loop of Henle — the countercurrent multiplier
Thin descending limb: permeable to water, not to salt → water leaves, fluid concentrates to ~1200 mOsm/kg at the tip of the loop.
Thick ascending limb: impermeable to water, actively pumps out Na+/K+/2Cl− (NKCC2) → fluid is diluted to ~100 mOsm/kg ("diluting segment").
This builds the medullary osmotic gradient (300 → 1200 mOsm/kg). Loop diuretics (furosemide) block NKCC2.
Aldosterone: increases Na+ reabsorption and K+ secretion in the principal cells.
ADH (vasopressin): inserts aquaporin-2 into the collecting duct → water moves out into the hypertonic medulla → concentrated urine (up to ~1200 mOsm/kg). Without ADH, dilute urine (~50–100 mOsm/kg).
Urine output ~1–2 L/day, i.e. >99% of the filtrate is reabsorbed.

steps.title: Filtration at the glomerulus
steps.say: Blood enters the glomerulus through the afferent arteriole and leaves through the efferent arteriole. Net filtration pressure is about 55 minus 15 minus 30, which is about 10 millimetres of mercury. GFR is about 125 millilitres per minute, roughly 180 litres a day, and the filtration fraction is about 20 percent.

steps.title: Efferent and afferent tone
steps.say: Constricting the efferent arteriole raises glomerular pressure and GFR. Constricting the afferent arteriole lowers both. This plate keeps both arterioles fixed, so it cannot show these changes.

steps.title: Proximal convoluted tubule
steps.say: The proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs about 65 percent of filtered sodium and water, all filtered glucose and amino acids, and about 80 percent of bicarbonate. This reabsorption is iso-osmotic, so the tubular fluid stays at about 300 milliosmoles per kilogram.

steps.title: Thin descending limb
steps.say: The thin descending limb is permeable to water but not to salt. Water leaves, so the fluid concentrates to about 1200 milliosmoles per kilogram at the tip of the loop.

steps.title: Thick ascending limb
steps.say: The thick ascending limb is impermeable to water and actively pumps out sodium, potassium and two chloride ions through NKCC2. The fluid is diluted to about 100 milliosmoles per kilogram, so this is called the diluting segment. This builds the medullary osmotic gradient from 300 to 1200 milliosmoles per kilogram. Loop diuretics like furosemide block NKCC2.

steps.title: Distal convoluted tubule
steps.say: The distal convoluted tubule reabsorbs sodium and chloride, and this is thiazide-sensitive.

steps.title: Aldosterone action
steps.say: Aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion in the principal cells of the collecting duct.

steps.title: ADH and concentrated urine
steps.say: ADH, also called vasopressin, inserts aquaporin-2 into the collecting duct. Water then moves out into the hypertonic medulla, making concentrated urine of up to about 1200 milliosmoles per kilogram. Without ADH, the urine is dilute at about 50 to 100 milliosmoles per kilogram.

steps.title: Key numbers
steps.say: Urine output is about 1 to 2 litres a day. That means more than 99 percent of the filtrate is reabsorbed.

extend: Dilute urine when ADH is off

overview.say: Blood enters the glomerulus through the afferent arteriole and leaves through the efferent arteriole, with a net filtration pressure of about 10 millimetres of mercury.
The proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs about 65 percent of filtered sodium and water, and the fluid stays iso-osmotic at about 300.
The thin descending limb is permeable to water but not salt, so the fluid concentrates to about 1200 at the loop tip.
The thick ascending limb is impermeable to water and pumps out sodium, potassium and chloride, diluting the fluid to about 100.
ADH inserts aquaporin-2 into the collecting duct, so water moves out into the hypertonic medulla and urine concentrates to about 1200.

exam.q: What is the net filtration pressure at the glomerulus?
exam.why: Net filtration pressure is about 55 minus 15 minus 30, which is about 10 millimetres of mercury.

exam.q: What fraction of filtered sodium and water does the proximal convoluted tubule reabsorb?
exam.why: The proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs about 65 percent of filtered sodium and water.

exam.q: What happens to the fluid in the thin descending limb?
options: Water leaves and the fluid concentrates to about 1200
Salt leaves and the fluid dilutes to about 100
Nothing leaves and the fluid stays at about 300
exam.why: The thin descending limb is permeable to water but not salt, so water leaves and the fluid concentrates to about 1200 milliosmoles per kilogram at the tip.

exam.q: Which transporter does the thick ascending limb use to pump out salt?
exam.why: The thick ascending limb actively pumps out sodium, potassium and two chloride ions through NKCC2.

exam.q: What does ADH do in the collecting duct?
options: Inserts aquaporin-2 so water moves out and urine concentrates
Blocks NKCC2 so salt stays in the lumen
Increases potassium secretion in principal cells
exam.why: ADH inserts aquaporin-2 into the collecting duct, so water moves out into the hypertonic medulla and urine concentrates to about 1200.
